verses.kjv: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
verses.modern: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, David remained two days in Ziklag.

verses.kjv: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
verses.modern: On the third day, a man came from Saul's camp, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and paid homage.

verses.kjv: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
verses.modern: David said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."

verses.kjv: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
verses.modern: David said to him, "How did it go? Tell me." And he answered, "The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people have fallen and are dead, and Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead."

verses.kjv: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
verses.modern: Then David said to the young man who told him, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"

verses.kjv: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
verses.modern: The young man who told him said, "By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, and the chariots and the horsemen were close upon him.

verses.kjv: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
verses.modern: When he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, 'Here I am.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
verses.modern: He said to me, 'Who are you?' I answered him, 'I am an Amalekite.'

verses.kjv: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.
verses.modern: He said to me, 'Stand beside me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and yet my life still lingers.'

verses.kjv: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
verses.modern: So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm. I have brought them here to my lord."

verses.kjv: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
verses.modern: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.

verses.kjv: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
verses.modern: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

verses.kjv: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
verses.modern: David said to the young man who told him, "Where do you come from?" And he answered, "I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite."

verses.kjv: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?
verses.modern: David said to him, "How is it you were not afraid to put out Your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?"

verses.kjv: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
verses.modern: Then David called one of the young men and said, "Go, execute him." And he struck him down so that he died.

verses.kjv: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD'S anointed.
verses.modern: David said to him, "Your blood be on your head, for Your own mouth has testified against You, saying, 'I have killed the LORD's anointed.' "

verses.kjv: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
verses.modern: David lamented with this lament over Saul and Jonathan his son,

verses.kjv: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
verses.modern: He said it should be taught to the people of Judah; it is written in the Book of Jasher. He said:

verses.kjv: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
verses.modern: "Your glory, O Israel, is slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!

verses.kjv: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
verses.modern: Tell it not in Gath, proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

verses.kjv: Ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.
verses.modern: You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fields of offerings! For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.

verses.kjv: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
verses.modern: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.

verses.kjv: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
verses.modern: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and lovely! In life and in death they were not divided; they were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.

verses.kjv: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
verses.modern: You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you luxuriously in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on your garments.

verses.kjv: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places.
verses.modern: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan lies slain on your high places.

verses.kjv: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
verses.modern: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; very pleasant have you been to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

verses.kjv: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
verses.modern: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war perished!"

chapters.summary: An Amalekite brought news of Saul's death to David, claiming he had killed Saul at his request; David ordered the man executed for striking the LORD's anointed. David composed a lament for Saul and Jonathan, mourning their deaths.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
verses.modern: After this David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?" And the LORD said to Him, "Go up." David said, "Where shall I go up?" And he said, "To Hebron."

verses.kjv: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal's wife the Carmelite.
verses.modern: So David went up there. His two wives also, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

verses.kjv: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
verses.modern: David brought up his men who were with him, every man with his household. They lived in the towns of Hebron.

verses.kjv: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabeshgilead were they that buried Saul.
verses.modern: The men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. When they told David, "It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul,"

verses.kjv: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabeshgilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of the LORD, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.
verses.modern: David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, "May You be blessed by the LORD, because You showed this loyalty to Saul your lord and buried him.

verses.kjv: And now the LORD shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
verses.modern: Now may the LORD show mercy and truth to You. And I will do good to You because You have done this thing.

verses.kjv: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
verses.modern: Now therefore let your hands be strong, and be valiant, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

verses.kjv: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
verses.modern: But Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim,

verses.kjv: And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.modern: He made him king over Gilead and the Ashurites and Jezreel and Ephraim and Benjamin and all Israel.

verses.kjv: Ishbosheth Saul's son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
verses.modern: Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel. He reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

verses.kjv: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.modern: The time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

verses.kjv: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.modern: Then Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
verses.modern: Joab the son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. And they sat down, the one on one side of the pool and the other on the other side of the pool.

verses.kjv: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
verses.modern: Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise and compete before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."

verses.kjv: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which pertained to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
verses.modern: Then they arose and crossed over by number, twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

verses.kjv: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow's side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkathhazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
verses.modern: Each caught his opponent by the head and thrust his sword in his opponent's side, so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is at Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
verses.modern: The battle was very fierce that day. And Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.

verses.kjv: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
verses.modern: The three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was as swift of foot as a wild gazelle.

verses.kjv: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
verses.modern: Asahel pursued Abner, and as he went he did not turn to the right or to the left from following Abner.

verses.kjv: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I am.
verses.modern: Then Abner looked behind him and said, "Is it you, Asahel?" And he answered, "It is I."

verses.kjv: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.
verses.modern: Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and seize one of the young men and take his spoil." But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

verses.kjv: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
verses.modern: Abner said again to Asahel, "Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift my face to your brother Joab?"

verses.kjv: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
verses.modern: But he refused to turn aside. Therefore Abner struck him in the stomach with the butt of his spear, so that the spear came out at his back. And he fell there and died where he was. And all who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died, stood still.

verses.kjv: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.modern: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. And as the sun was going down they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.
verses.modern: The people of Benjamin gathered themselves together behind Abner and became one group and stood on top of a hill.

verses.kjv: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
verses.modern: Then Abner called to Joab, "Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that the end will be bitter? How long will it be before you tell your people to turn from the pursuit of their brothers?"

verses.kjv: And Joab said, As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.
verses.modern: Joab said, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, surely the men would not have given up the pursuit of their brothers until the morning."

verses.kjv: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
verses.modern: So Joab blew the trumpet. All the people stopped and pursued Israel no further. They did not fight anymore.

verses.kjv: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
verses.modern: Abner and his men went all that night through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan and, marching the whole morning, they came to Mahanaim.

verses.kjv: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel.
verses.modern: Joab returned from the pursuit of Abner. And when he had gathered all the people together, there were missing from David's servants nineteen men besides Asahel.

verses.kjv: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, so that three hundred and threescore men died.
verses.modern: But the servants of David had struck down of Benjamin three hundred and sixty of Abner's men.

verses.kjv: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.
verses.modern: They took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was at Bethlehem. And Joab and his men marched all night, and the day broke upon them at Hebron.

chapters.summary: David was anointed king over Judah at Hebron, while Abner made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over the rest of Israel. War broke out between the two houses, and at the battle of Gibeon, Abner killed Joab's brother Asahel.

verses.kjv: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.
verses.modern: There was a long war between the house of Saul and the house of David. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul became weaker and weaker.

verses.kjv: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
verses.modern: Sons were born to David at Hebron: his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam of Jezreel;

verses.kjv: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
verses.modern: His second, Chileab, of Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel. The third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

verses.kjv: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
verses.modern: The fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith. The fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

verses.kjv: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.modern: The sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.
verses.modern: While there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.

verses.kjv: And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ishbosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father's concubine?
verses.modern: Now Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. And Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

verses.kjv: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ishbosheth, and said, Am I a dog's head, which against Judah do shew kindness this day unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?
verses.modern: Then Abner was very angry over the words of Ish-bosheth and said, "Am I a dog's head of Judah? To this day I keep showing loyalty to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and his friends, and have not given you into the hand of David. And yet you charge me today with a fault concerning a woman.

verses.kjv: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;
verses.modern: God do so to Abner and more also, if I do not accomplish for David what the LORD has sworn to Him,

verses.kjv: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.
verses.modern: To transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."

verses.kjv: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.
verses.modern: Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.

verses.kjv: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.
verses.modern: Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, "To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and my hand shall be with you to bring over all Israel to you."

verses.kjv: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
verses.modern: He said, "Good; I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I require of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see my face."

verses.kjv: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth Saul's son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
verses.modern: Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, for whom I paid the bride-price of a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."

verses.kjv: And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish.
verses.modern: Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband Paltiel the son of Laish.

verses.kjv: And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned.
verses.modern: But her husband went with her, weeping after her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go, return." And he returned.

verses.kjv: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past to be king over you:
verses.modern: Abner conferred with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time past you have been seeking David as king over you.

verses.kjv: Now then do it: for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
verses.modern: Now then bring it about, for the LORD has promised David, saying, 'By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and from the hand of all their enemies.' "

verses.kjv: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.modern: Abner also spoke to Benjamin. And then Abner went to tell David at Hebron all that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin thought good to do.

verses.kjv: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.
verses.modern: When Abner came with twenty men to David at Hebron, David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

verses.kjv: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thine heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
verses.modern: Abner said to David, "I will arise and go and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may reign over all that your heart desires." So David sent Abner away. He went in peace.

verses.kjv: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from pursuing a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
verses.modern: Just then the servants of David arrived with Joab from a raid, bringing much spoil with them. But Abner was not with David at Hebron, for he had sent him away. He had gone in peace.

verses.kjv: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
verses.modern: When Joab and all the army with him came, it was told Joab, "Abner the son of Ner came to the king. He sent him away. He has gone in peace."

verses.kjv: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
verses.modern: Then Joab went to the king and said, "What have you done? See, Abner came to you. Why did you let him go, so that he is already gone?

verses.kjv: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
verses.modern: You know that Abner the son of Ner came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing."

verses.kjv: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, which brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
verses.modern: When Joab came out from David's presence, he sent messengers after Abner. They brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But David did not know about it.

verses.kjv: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
verses.modern: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him privately, and there he struck him in the stomach so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

verses.kjv: And afterward when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
verses.modern: Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, "I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the LORD for the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

verses.kjv: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father's house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the sword, or that lacketh bread.
verses.modern: May it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house, and may the house of Joab never be without one who has a discharge or who is leprous or who holds a spindle or who falls by the sword or who lacks bread!"

verses.kjv: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.modern: So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because He had put their brother Asahel to death in the battle at Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David himself followed the bier.
verses.modern: Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your clothes and put on sackcloth and mourn before Abner." And King David followed the bier.

verses.kjv: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
verses.modern: They buried Abner at Hebron. And the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner. All the people wept.

verses.kjv: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dieth?
verses.modern: The king lamented for Abner, saying, "Should Abner die as a fool dies?

verses.kjv: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, so fellest thou. And all the people wept again over him.
verses.modern: Your hands were not bound; your feet were not fettered. As one falls before the wicked, you have fallen." And all the people wept again over him.

verses.kjv: And when all the people came to cause David to eat meat while it was yet day, David sware, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or ought else, till the sun be down.
verses.modern: Then all the people came to persuade David to eat bread while it was still day. But David swore, saying, "God do so to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else until the sun goes down!"

verses.kjv: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them: as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.
verses.modern: All the people took notice of it. It pleased them, as everything the king did pleased all the people.

verses.kjv: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
verses.modern: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it had not been the king's will to put to death Abner the son of Ner.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
verses.modern: The king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?

verses.kjv: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah be too hard for me: the LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.
verses.modern: I am this day weak, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah, are more severe than I. The LORD repay the evildoer according to His wickedness!"

chapters.summary: Abner defected from Ish-bosheth to David and began rallying the tribes to David's side. Joab murdered Abner at Hebron in revenge for Asahel, and David publicly mourned Abner and cursed Joab's house.

verses.kjv: And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
verses.modern: When Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, heard that Abner had died at Hebron, his courage failed. All Israel was dismayed.

verses.kjv: And Saul's son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:
verses.modern: Now Saul's son had two men who were commanders of raiding bands; the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon a man of Benjamin from Beeroth (for Beeroth also is counted part of Benjamin;

verses.kjv: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
verses.modern: The Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have been sojourners there to this day).

verses.kjv: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
verses.modern: Jonathan, the son of Saul, had a son who was crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse took him up and fled, and as she fled in her haste, he fell and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
verses.modern: Now the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, set out, and about the heat of the day they came to the house of Ish-bosheth as he was taking his midday rest.

verses.kjv: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
verses.modern: They came into the midst of the house as if to get wheat. They stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

verses.kjv: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.
verses.modern: When they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedroom, they struck him and put him to death and beheaded him. They took his head and went by the way of the Arabah all night,

verses.kjv: And they brought the head of Ishbosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ishbosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
verses.modern: Brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron. And they said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his seed."

verses.kjv: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
verses.modern: But David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life out of every adversity,

verses.kjv: When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
verses.modern: When one told me, 'See, Saul is dead,' and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his news.

verses.kjv: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
verses.modern: How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed, shall I not now require his blood at your hand and destroy you from the earth?"

verses.kjv: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth, and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.
verses.modern: David commanded his young men. They killed them and cut off their hands and feet and hanged them beside the pool at Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner at Hebron.

chapters.summary: Two of Ish-bosheth's captains, Rechab and Baanah, assassinated him in his bed and brought his head to David. David had them executed for killing an innocent man and buried Ish-bosheth's head in Abner's tomb at Hebron.

verses.kjv: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
verses.modern: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "See, we are your bone and flesh.

verses.kjv: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.
verses.modern: In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. And the LORD said to You, 'You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and You shall be prince over Israel.' "

verses.kjv: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD: and they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.modern: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. They anointed David king over Israel.

verses.kjv: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
verses.modern: David was thirty years old when he began to reign. He reigned forty years.

verses.kjv: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.modern: At Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and at Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah thirty-three years.

verses.kjv: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither.
verses.modern: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who said to David, "You will not come in here, but the blind and the lame will ward you off"—thinking, "David cannot come in here."

verses.kjv: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.
verses.modern: Nevertheless, David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.

verses.kjv: And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David's soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.
verses.modern: David said on that day, "Whoever would strike the Jebusites, let him get up the water shaft to attack 'the lame and the blind,' who are hated by David's soul." Therefore it is said, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."

verses.kjv: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.
verses.modern: David lived in the stronghold and called it the city of David. And David built the city all around from the Millo inward.

verses.kjv: And David went on, and grew great, and the LORD God of hosts was with him.
verses.modern: David became greater and greater, for the LORD, the God of hosts, was with Him.

verses.kjv: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David an house.
verses.modern: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and also carpenters and masons who built David a house.

verses.kjv: And David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.
verses.modern: David knew that the LORD had established Him king over Israel, and that He had exalted His kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.

verses.kjv: And David took him more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.
verses.modern: David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.

verses.kjv: And these be the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
verses.modern: These are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

verses.kjv: Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
verses.modern: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

verses.kjv: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
verses.modern: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

verses.kjv: But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the hold.
verses.modern: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to search for David. But David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.

verses.kjv: The Philistines also came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.modern: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv: And David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? And the LORD said unto David, Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand.
verses.modern: David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You give them into my hand?" And the LORD said to David, "Go up, for I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand."

verses.kjv: And David came to Baalperazim, and David smote them there, and said, The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baalperazim.
verses.modern: David came to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. And he said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breaking flood." Therefore the name of that place is called Baal-perazim.

verses.kjv: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them.
verses.modern: The Philistines left their idols there, and David and his men burned them.

verses.kjv: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.modern: The Philistines came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv: And when David enquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.
verses.modern: When David inquired of the LORD, He said, "You shall not go up; go around to their rear, and come against them opposite the balsam trees.

verses.kjv: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.
verses.modern: When You hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then rouse Yourself, for then the LORD has gone out before You to strike down the army of the Philistines."

verses.kjv: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gazer.
verses.modern: David did as the LORD commanded Him, and struck down the Philistines from Geba to Gezer.

chapters.summary: All the tribes of Israel came to Hebron and anointed David king over all Israel. David captured the Jebusite stronghold of Jerusalem and made it his capital, and he defeated the Philistines twice in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv: Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.modern: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

verses.kjv: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims.
verses.modern: David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the name of the LORD of hosts who sits enthroned on the cherubim.

verses.kjv: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.
verses.modern: They carried the ark of God on a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.

verses.kjv: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
verses.modern: They brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio went before the ark.

verses.kjv: And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
verses.modern: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD, with songs and lyres and harps and tambourines and castanets and cymbals.

verses.kjv: And when they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.
verses.modern: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah put out His hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.

verses.kjv: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
verses.modern: The anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah. God struck Him down there because of His error. He died there beside the ark of God.

verses.kjv: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perezuzzah to this day.
verses.modern: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah. And that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.

verses.kjv: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?
verses.modern: David was afraid of the LORD that day. He said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"

verses.kjv: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.
verses.modern: So David was not willing to take the ark of the LORD into the city of David. But David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

verses.kjv: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obededom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obededom, and all his household.
verses.modern: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months. The LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

verses.kjv: And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obededom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obededom into the city of David with gladness.
verses.modern: It was told King David, "The LORD has blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that belongs to Him, because of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the city of David with rejoicing.

verses.kjv: And it was so, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
verses.modern: When those who bore the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, He sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.

verses.kjv: And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
verses.modern: David danced before the LORD with all His might. And David was wearing a linen ephod.

verses.kjv: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
verses.modern: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the horn.

verses.kjv: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.modern: As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD. She despised Him in her heart.

verses.kjv: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
verses.modern: They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place, inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

verses.kjv: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
verses.modern: When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, He blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts

verses.kjv: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.
verses.modern: Distributed among all the people, the whole crowd of Israel, both men and women, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins to each one. Then all the people departed, each to his house.

verses.kjv: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!
verses.modern: David returned to bless his household. But Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel honored himself today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants' female servants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"

verses.kjv: And David said unto Michal, It was before the LORD, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.
verses.modern: David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, Who chose me above Your father and above all His house, to appoint me as prince over Israel, the people of the LORD—and I will celebrate before the LORD.

verses.kjv: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.
verses.modern: I will make myself yet more contemptible than this. I will be abased in Your eyes. But by the female servants of whom You have spoken, by them I shall be held in honor."

verses.kjv: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
verses.modern: Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

chapters.summary: David brought the ark of God toward Jerusalem, but Uzzah was struck dead for touching it, and David left the ark at the house of Obed-edom. Three months later David brought the ark into Jerusalem with dancing and celebration; Michal despised him and was left childless.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest round about from all his enemies;
verses.modern: Now when the king lived in his house and the LORD had given Him rest from all His surrounding enemies,

verses.kjv: That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.
verses.modern: The king said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells in a tent."

verses.kjv: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thine heart; for the LORD is with thee.
verses.modern: Nathan said to the king, "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with You."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan, saying,
verses.modern: But that same night the word of the LORD came to Nathan,

verses.kjv: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?
verses.modern: "Go and tell my servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: Would You build me a house to dwell in?

verses.kjv: Whereas I have not dwelt in any house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.modern: I have not lived in a house since the day I brought up the people of Israel from Egypt to this day. But I have been moving about in a tent for my dwelling.

verses.kjv: In all the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?
verses.modern: In all places where I have moved with all the people of Israel, did I speak a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, "Why have You not built me a house of cedar?"'

verses.kjv: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
verses.modern: Now, therefore, thus You shall say to my servant David, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts, I took You from the pasture, from following the sheep, that You should be prince over my people Israel.

verses.kjv: And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great men that are in the earth.
verses.modern: I have been with You wherever You went and have cut off all Your enemies from before You. And I will make for You a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth.

verses.kjv: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,
verses.modern: I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. And violent men shall afflict them no more, as formerly,

verses.kjv: And as since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee an house.
verses.modern: From the time that I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give You rest from all Your enemies. Moreover, the LORD declares to You that the LORD will make You a house.

verses.kjv: And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.modern: When Your days are fulfilled and You lie down with Your fathers, I will raise up Your seed after You, who shall come from Your body. I will establish His kingdom.

verses.kjv: He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
verses.modern: He shall build a house for my name. I will establish the throne of His kingdom forever.

verses.kjv: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:
verses.modern: I will be to Him a father. He shall be to me a son. If He commit iniquity, I will discipline Him with the rod of men, with the stripes of the sons of men,

verses.kjv: But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee.
verses.modern: But my mercy will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away from before you.

verses.kjv: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
verses.modern: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before thee. Your throne shall be established forever.' "

verses.kjv: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.
verses.modern: In accordance with all these words, and in accordance with all this vision, Nathan spoke to David.

verses.kjv: Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?
verses.modern: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me thus far?

verses.kjv: And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord GOD; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant's house for a great while to come. And is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
verses.modern: Yet this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD. You have spoken also of Your servant's house for a great while to come, and is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD!

verses.kjv: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant.
verses.modern: What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, O Lord GOD!

verses.kjv: For thy word's sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know them.
verses.modern: Because of Your promise, and according to Your own heart, You have brought about all this greatness, to make Your servant know it.

verses.kjv: Wherefore thou art great, O LORD God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.modern: Therefore You are great, O LORD God. For there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

verses.kjv: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people, which thou redeemedst to thee from Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
verses.modern: Who is like Your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem to be His people, making Himself a name and doing for them great and awesome things by driving out before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, a nation and its gods?

verses.kjv: For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever: and thou, LORD, art become their God.
verses.modern: You established for Yourself Your people Israel to be Your people forever. And You, O LORD, became their God.

verses.kjv: And now, O LORD God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish it for ever, and do as thou hast said.
verses.modern: Now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning His house, and do as You have spoken.

verses.kjv: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts is the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.
verses.modern: Your name will be magnified forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel,' and the house of Your servant David will be established before you.

verses.kjv: For thou, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee an house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.
verses.modern: For You, O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have made this revelation to Your servant, saying, 'I will build You a house.' Therefore Your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to You.

verses.kjv: And now, O Lord GOD, thou art that God, and thy words be true, and thou hast promised this goodness unto thy servant:
verses.modern: Now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are true, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.

verses.kjv: Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord GOD, hast spoken it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.
verses.modern: Now therefore may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, so that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing shall the house of Your servant be blessed forever."

chapters.summary: David desired to build a house for the LORD, but God sent Nathan the prophet to tell him that his son would build the temple. The LORD made a covenant with David, promising that his throne would be established forever.

verses.kjv: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Methegammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
verses.modern: After this David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.

verses.kjv: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David's servants, and brought gifts.
verses.modern: He defeated Moab and he measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. Two lines he measured to be put to death, and one full line to be spared. And the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.

verses.kjv: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.
verses.modern: David also defeated Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his power at the river Euphrates.

verses.kjv: And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for an hundred chariots.
verses.modern: David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen. And David hamstrung all the chariot horses but left enough for a hundred chariots.

verses.kjv: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.
verses.modern: When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down 22,000 men of the Syrians.

verses.kjv: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
verses.modern: Then David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to David and brought tribute. And the LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.

verses.kjv: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: David took the shields of gold that were carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
verses.modern: From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took very much bronze.

verses.kjv: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
verses.modern: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer,

verses.kjv: Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
verses.modern: Toi sent his son Joram to King David, to ask about his health and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him, for Hadadezer had often been at war with Toi. And Joram brought with him articles of silver, gold, and bronze.

verses.kjv: Which also king David did dedicate unto the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
verses.modern: These also King David dedicated to the LORD, together with the silver and gold that He dedicated from all the nations he subdued—

verses.kjv: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.modern: From Syria, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

verses.kjv: And David gat him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, being eighteen thousand men.
verses.modern: David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

verses.kjv: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
verses.modern: Then He put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom He put garrisons. All the Edomites became David's servants. And the LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.

verses.kjv: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.
verses.modern: So David reigned over all Israel. And David administered justice and equity to all his people.

verses.kjv: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
verses.modern: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder,

verses.kjv: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;
verses.modern: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was secretary,

verses.kjv: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.
verses.modern: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and David's sons were chief rulers.

chapters.summary: David defeated the Philistines, Moabites, the king of Zobah, the Syrians, and the Edomites, extending his kingdom in every direction. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went, and David administered justice over all Israel.

verses.kjv: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan's sake?
verses.modern: David said, "Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?"

verses.kjv: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
verses.modern: Now there was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba. And when they called him to David, the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "I am your servant."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
verses.modern: The king said, "Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to Him?" Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan; he is crippled in his feet."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar.
verses.modern: The king said to him, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, at Lodebar."

verses.kjv: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.
verses.modern: Then King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

verses.kjv: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
verses.modern: Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to David and fell on his face and paid homage. And David said, "Mephibosheth!" And he answered, "Here is your servant."

verses.kjv: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
verses.modern: David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you shall eat at my table always."

verses.kjv: And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
verses.modern: He paid homage and said, "What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog such as I?"

verses.kjv: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master's son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.
verses.modern: Then the king called Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.

verses.kjv: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master's son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.modern: You and your sons and your servants shall till the land for him and shall bring in the produce, that your master's son may have bread to eat. But Mephibosheth your master's son shall always eat at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

verses.kjv: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.
verses.modern: Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so will your servant do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table, like one of the king's sons.

verses.kjv: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha: and all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
verses.modern: Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. And all who lived in Ziba's house became Mephibosheth's servants.

verses.kjv: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king's table; and was lame on both his feet.
verses.modern: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he always ate at the king's table. Now he was lame in both his feet.

chapters.summary: David sought out any remaining member of Saul's house to show kindness for Jonathan's sake. He found Mephibosheth, Jonathan's crippled son, restored all of Saul's land to him, and gave him a permanent place at the king's table.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
verses.modern: After this the king of the Ammonites died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

verses.kjv: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
verses.modern: David said, "I will deal loyally with Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father dealt loyally with me." So David sent by his servants to console him concerning his father. And David's servants came into the land of the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David rather sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
verses.modern: But the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think, because David has sent comforters to you, that he is honoring your father? Has not David sent his servants to you to search the city and to spy it out and to overthrow it?"

verses.kjv: Wherefore Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.modern: So Hanun took David's servants and shaved off half the beard of each and cut off their garments in the middle, at their hips, and sent them away.

verses.kjv: When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.
verses.modern: When it was told David, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, "Remain at Jericho until your beards have grown and then return."

verses.kjv: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Bethrehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ishtob twelve thousand men.
verses.modern: When the Ammonites saw that they had become a stench to David, the Ammonites sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob and the Syrians of Zobah, 20,000 foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah with 1,000 men, and the men of Tob, 12,000 men.

verses.kjv: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
verses.modern: When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.

verses.kjv: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
verses.modern: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the gate, and the Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.

verses.kjv: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:
verses.modern: When Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Syrians.

verses.kjv: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put them in array against the children of Ammon.
verses.modern: The rest of his men he put in the charge of Abishai his brother. He arrayed them against the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
verses.modern: He said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me, but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.

verses.kjv: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.
verses.modern: Be strong, and let us be courageous for the sake of our people, and for the cities of our God, and may the LORD do what seems good to Him."

verses.kjv: And Joab drew nigh, and the people that were with him, unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
verses.modern: So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Syrians. They fled before Him.

verses.kjv: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled, they likewise fled before Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
verses.modern: But when the Syrians saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they gathered themselves together.

verses.kjv: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.
verses.modern: Hadarezer sent and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the Euphrates. They came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of the army of Hadarezer at their head.

verses.kjv: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
verses.modern: When it was told David, he gathered all Israel together and crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. The Syrians arrayed themselves against David and fought with him.

verses.kjv: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew the men of seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.
verses.modern: The Syrians fled before Israel, and David killed of the Syrians the men of 700 chariots, and 40,000 horsemen, and struck down Shobach the commander of their army, so that he died there.

verses.kjv: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
verses.modern: When all the kings who were servants of Hadarezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. So the Syrians were afraid to save the Ammonites anymore.

chapters.summary: David sent envoys to comfort the new king of Ammon, but they were humiliated by having their beards half shaved and garments cut. The Ammonites hired Syrian mercenaries, but Joab and Abishai defeated both the Ammonites and the Syrians.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
verses.modern: In the spring of the year, the time when kings go out to battle, David sent Joab. His servants with him. All Israel. And they ravaged the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David remained at Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
verses.modern: It happened, late one afternoon, when David arose from his couch and was walking on the roof of the king's house, that he saw from the roof a woman bathing. The woman was very beautiful.

verses.kjv: And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
verses.modern: David sent and inquired about the woman. And one said, "Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"

verses.kjv: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
