verses.modern: So David sent messengers and took her. She came to him. He lay with her. (Now she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness.) Then she returned to her house.

verses.kjv: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
verses.modern: The woman conceived. She sent and told David, "I am pregnant."

verses.kjv: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.modern: So David sent word to Joab, "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.

verses.kjv: And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
verses.modern: When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab was doing and how the people were doing and how the war was going.

verses.kjv: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.
verses.modern: Then David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." And Uriah went out of the king's house, and there followed him a present from the king.

verses.kjv: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
verses.modern: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.

verses.kjv: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down unto thine house?
verses.modern: When they told David, "Uriah did not go down to his house," David said to Uriah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"

verses.kjv: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
verses.modern: Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in booths, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are camping in the open field. Shall I then go to my house, to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing."

verses.kjv: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
verses.modern: Then David said to Uriah, "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you back." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next.

verses.kjv: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
verses.modern: David invited him. He ate in his presence and drank, so that he made him drunk. And in the evening he went out to lie on his couch with the servants of his lord. But he did not go down to his house.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.modern: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

verses.kjv: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
verses.modern: In the letter he wrote, "Set Uriah in the forefront of the hardest fighting, and then draw back from him, that he may be struck down and die."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.
verses.modern: As Joab was besieging the city, he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew there were valiant men.

verses.kjv: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
verses.modern: The men of the city came out and fought with Joab. Some of the servants of David fell. Uriah the Hittite also died.

verses.kjv: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
verses.modern: Then Joab sent and told David all the news about the fighting.

verses.kjv: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
verses.modern: He instructed the messenger, "When you have finished telling all the news about the fighting to the king,

verses.kjv: And if so be that the king's wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
verses.modern: Then if the king's anger rises, and if he says to you, 'Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

verses.kjv: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.modern: Who killed Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.' "

verses.kjv: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.
verses.modern: So the messenger went and came and told David all that Joab had sent him to tell.

verses.kjv: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.
verses.modern: The messenger said to David, "The men gained an advantage over us and came out against us in the field. But we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.

verses.kjv: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king's servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.modern: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall. Some of the king's servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also."

verses.kjv: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
verses.modern: David said to the messenger, "Thus shall you say to Joab, 'Do not let this matter displease you, for the sword devours now one and now another. Strengthen your attack against the city and overthrow it.' And encourage him."

verses.kjv: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
verses.modern: When the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she lamented over her husband.

verses.kjv: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
verses.modern: When the mourning was over, David sent and brought her to his house. She became his wife and bore Him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.

chapters.summary: David committed adultery with Bathsheba while her husband Uriah was at war, and she became pregnant. When David's attempts to cover the sin failed, he ordered Joab to place Uriah in the fiercest fighting, where he was killed.

verses.kjv: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
verses.modern: The LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said to him, "There were two men in a certain city, the one rich and the other poor.

verses.kjv: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
verses.modern: The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

verses.kjv: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
verses.modern: But the poor man had nothing but one little ewe lamb, which he had bought. And he brought it up. It grew up with him and with his children. It used to eat of his morsel and drink from his cup and lie in his arms. It was like a daughter to him.

verses.kjv: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
verses.modern: Now there came a traveler to the rich man. He was unwilling to take one of his own flock or herd to prepare for the guest who had come to him. But he took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."

verses.kjv: And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
verses.modern: Then David's anger was greatly kindled against the man. He said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who has done this deserves to die,

verses.kjv: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
verses.modern: He shall restore the lamb fourfold, because He did this thing, and because He had no pity."

verses.kjv: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
verses.modern: Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, 'I anointed you king over Israel. I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

verses.kjv: And I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.
verses.modern: I gave You Your master's house and Your master's wives into Your arms and gave You the house of Israel and of Judah. And if this were too little, I would add to You as much more.

verses.kjv: Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
verses.modern: Why have You despised the word of the LORD, to do what is evil in His sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and have taken his wife to be Your wife and have killed Him with the sword of the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
verses.modern: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from Your house, because You have despised me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.modern: Thus says the LORD, ' I will raise up evil against You out of Your own house. And I will take Your wives before Your eyes and give them to Your neighbor. He shall lie with Your wives in the sight of this sun.

verses.kjv: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
verses.modern: For You did it secretly. But I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.' "

verses.kjv: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
verses.modern: David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan said to David, "The LORD also has put away your sin; you shall not die.

verses.kjv: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
verses.modern: Nevertheless, because by this deed You have utterly scorned the LORD, the child who is born to you shall die."

verses.kjv: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
verses.modern: Then Nathan went to his house. And the LORD afflicted the child that Uriah's wife bore to David. He became sick.

verses.kjv: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
verses.modern: David therefore sought God on behalf of the child. And David fasted and went in and lay all night on the ground.

verses.kjv: And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
verses.modern: The elders of his house stood beside him, to raise him from the ground. But he would not, nor did he eat food with them.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
verses.modern: On the seventh day the child died. And the servants of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "While the child was still alive, we spoke to him. He did not listen to us. How then can we say to him the child is dead? He may do himself some harm."

verses.kjv: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
verses.modern: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David understood that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" They said, "He is dead."

verses.kjv: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
verses.modern: Then David arose from the earth and washed and anointed Himself and changed His clothes and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. He then went to His own house. And when He asked, they set food before Him. He ate.

verses.kjv: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
verses.modern: Then His servants said to him, "What is this thing that You have done? You fasted and wept for the child while it was alive, but when the child died, you arose and ate food."

verses.kjv: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
verses.modern: He said, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?'

verses.kjv: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
verses.modern: But now He is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring Him back again? I shall go to Him. But He will not return to me."

verses.kjv: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
verses.modern: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and went in to her and lay with her. She bore a son. He called His name Solomon. And the LORD loved Him

verses.kjv: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
verses.modern: Sent a message by Nathan the prophet. So he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
verses.modern: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal city.

verses.kjv: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
verses.modern: Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah; moreover, I have taken the city of waters.

verses.kjv: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
verses.modern: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together and encamp against the city and take it, lest I take the city and it be called by my name."

verses.kjv: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
verses.modern: So David gathered all the people together and went to Rabbah and fought against it and took it.

verses.kjv: And he took their king's crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
verses.modern: He took the crown of their king from his head. The weight of it was a talent of gold, and in it was a precious stone. It was placed on David's head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.

verses.kjv: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
verses.modern: He brought out the people who were in it and set them to labor with saws and iron picks and iron axes and made them toil at the brick kilns. And thus he did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

chapters.summary: Nathan the prophet confronted David with a parable about a rich man who stole a poor man's lamb, and David condemned himself. God declared that the sword would never depart from David's house; the child born of the adultery died, but Bathsheba later bore Solomon.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
verses.modern: Now Absalom, David's son, had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar. And Amnon the son of David loved her.

verses.kjv: And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
verses.modern: Amnon was so tormented that he made himself ill because of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin. It seemed impossible to Amnon to do anything to her.

verses.kjv: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother: and Jonadab was a very subtil man.
verses.modern: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother. And Jonadab was a very crafty man.

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Why art thou, being the king's son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.
verses.modern: He said to him, "O son of the king, why are you so haggard morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" Amnon told him, "I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."

verses.kjv: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it at her hand.
verses.modern: Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat it from her hand.' "

verses.kjv: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
verses.modern: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. And when the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand."

verses.kjv: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon's house, and dress him meat.
verses.modern: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, "Go to your brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him."

verses.kjv: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.
verses.modern: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down. And she took dough and kneaded it and made cakes in his sight and baked the cakes.

verses.kjv: And she took a pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.
verses.modern: She took the pan and poured them out before him. But he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send out everyone from me." So everyone went out from him.

verses.kjv: And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
verses.modern: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.

verses.kjv: And when she had brought them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.
verses.modern: But when she brought them near him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."

verses.kjv: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
verses.modern: She answered him, "No, my brother, do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel; do not do this outrageous thing.

verses.kjv: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.
verses.modern: As for me, where could I carry my shame? And as for you, you would be as one of the outrageous fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."

verses.kjv: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.
verses.modern: But he would not listen to her, and being stronger than she, he violated her and lay with her.

verses.kjv: Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.
verses.modern: Then Amnon hated her with very great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up! Go!"

verses.kjv: And she said unto him, There is no cause: this evil in sending me away is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.
verses.modern: But she said to him, "No, my brother, for this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other that you did to me." But he would not listen to her.

verses.kjv: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
verses.modern: He called the young man who served him and said, "Put this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her."

verses.kjv: And she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
verses.modern: Now she was wearing a long robe with sleeves, for thus were the virgin daughters of the king dressed. So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her.

verses.kjv: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.
verses.modern: Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe that she wore. And she laid her hand on her head and went away, crying aloud as she went.

verses.kjv: And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house.
verses.modern: Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother; do not take this to heart." So Tamar lived, a desolate woman, in her brother Absalom's house.

verses.kjv: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.
verses.modern: When King David heard of all these things, he was very angry.

verses.kjv: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
verses.modern: But Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had violated his sister Tamar.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
verses.modern: After two full years Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons.

verses.kjv: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.
verses.modern: Absalom came to the king and said, "See, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant."

verses.kjv: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.
verses.modern: But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you." He pressed him. But he would not go but gave him his blessing.

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?
verses.modern: Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"

verses.kjv: But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.
verses.modern: But Absalom pressed him until he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

verses.kjv: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.
verses.modern: Then Absalom commanded his servants, "Mark when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then kill him. Do not fear; have I not commanded you? Be courageous and be valiant."

verses.kjv: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.
verses.modern: So the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and each mounted his mule and fled.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left.
verses.modern: While they were on the way, news came to David, "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left."

verses.kjv: Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.
verses.modern: Then the king arose and tore his garments and lay on the earth. And all his servants who were standing by tore their garments.

verses.kjv: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men the king's sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
verses.modern: But Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men the king's sons, for Amnon alone is dead. For by the command of Absalom this has been determined from the day he violated his sister Tamar.

verses.kjv: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king's sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.
verses.modern: Now therefore let not my lord the king so take it to heart as to think that all the king's sons are dead, for Amnon alone is dead."

verses.kjv: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill side behind him.
verses.modern: But Absalom fled. And the young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and there came much people by the road behind him by the side of the mountain.

verses.kjv: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king's sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.
verses.modern: Jonadab said to the king, "See, the king's sons have come; as your servant said, so it is."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.
verses.modern: As soon as he had finished speaking, the king's sons came and lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also and all his servants wept very bitterly.

verses.kjv: But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
verses.modern: But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son day after day.

verses.kjv: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
verses.modern: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

verses.kjv: And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.
verses.modern: The soul of the king longed to go out to Absalom, because he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.

chapters.summary: David's son Amnon raped his half-sister Tamar, and David was furious but did nothing. Two years later, Absalom avenged Tamar by having his servants kill Amnon at a feast, then fled to Geshur.

verses.kjv: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom.
verses.modern: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart went out to Absalom.

verses.kjv: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
verses.modern: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman and said to her, "Please pretend to be a mourner, and put on mourning garments. Do not anoint yourself with oil, but behave like a woman who has been mourning many days for the dead.

verses.kjv: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.
verses.modern: Go to the king and speak to him in this way." And Joab put the words in her mouth.

verses.kjv: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
verses.modern: When the woman of Tekoa came to the king, she fell on her face to the ground and paid homage and said, "Help, O king!"

verses.kjv: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.
verses.modern: The king said to her, "What is your trouble?" She answered, "Alas, I am a widow; my husband is dead.

verses.kjv: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.
verses.modern: Your servant had two sons. They quarreled with one another in the field. There was no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.

verses.kjv: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the earth.
verses.modern: Now the whole clan has risen against your servant. They say, 'Give up the man who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed.' And so they would destroy the heir also. Thus they would quench my coal that is left and leave to my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the earth."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.
verses.modern: Then the king said to the woman, "Go to your house. I will give orders concerning you."

verses.kjv: And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father's house: and the king and his throne be guiltless.
verses.modern: The woman of Tekoa said to the king, "On me be the guilt, my lord the king, and on my father's house; let the king and his throne be guiltless."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Whosoever saith ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.
verses.modern: The king said, "If anyone says anything to you, bring him to me. He shall never touch you again."

verses.kjv: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
verses.modern: Then she said, "Please let the king invoke the LORD Your God, that the avenger of blood kill no more, and my son not be destroyed." He said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of Your son shall fall to the ground."

verses.kjv: Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak one word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
verses.modern: Then the woman said, "Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."

verses.kjv: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.
verses.modern: The woman said, "Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in giving this decision the king convicts himself, inasmuch as the king does not bring his banished one home again.

verses.kjv: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
verses.modern: We must all die; we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. Yet God doth not respect any person. He devises means so that the banished one will not remain an outcast.

verses.kjv: Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
verses.modern: Now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid, and your servant thought, 'I will speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.

verses.kjv: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
verses.modern: For the king will hear and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the heritage of God.'

verses.kjv: Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.
verses.modern: Your servant thought, 'The word of my lord the king will set me at rest,' for my lord the king is like the angel of God to discern good and evil. The LORD Your God be with You!"

verses.kjv: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.
verses.modern: Then the king answered the woman, "Do not hide from me anything I ask you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:
verses.modern: The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered and said, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, one cannot turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has said. It was your servant Joab who commanded me; it was he who put all these words in the mouth of your servant.

verses.kjv: To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.
verses.modern: In order to change the course of things your servant Joab did this. But my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God to know all things that are on earth."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.
verses.modern: Then the king said to Joab, "See now, I grant this; go, bring back the young man Absalom."

verses.kjv: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
verses.modern: Joab fell on his face to the ground and paid homage and blessed the king. And Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has granted the request of his servant."

verses.kjv: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: So Joab arose and went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king's face.
verses.modern: The king said, "Let him dwell apart in his own house; he is not to come into my presence." So Absalom lived apart in his own house and did not come into the king's presence.

verses.kjv: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.modern: Now in all Israel there was no one so much to be praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

verses.kjv: And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year's end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.
verses.modern: When he cut the hair of his head (for at the end of every year he used to cut it; when it was heavy on him, he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head, two hundred shekels by the king's weight.

verses.kjv: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
verses.modern: There were born to Absalom three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a woman of a fair countenance.

verses.kjv: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king's face.
verses.modern: So Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, without coming into the king's presence.

verses.kjv: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
verses.modern: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but Joab would not come to him. And he sent a second time, but Joab would not come.

verses.kjv: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab's field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
verses.modern: Then he said to his servants, "See, Joab's field is next to mine. He has barley there; go and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the field on fire.

verses.kjv: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
verses.modern: Then Joab arose and came to Absalom at his house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

verses.kjv: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king's face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
verses.modern: Absalom answered Joab, "I sent word to you, 'Come here, that I may send you to the king, to ask, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to still be there."' Now therefore let me see the king's face, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death."

verses.kjv: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.modern: Then Joab went to the king and told him. And he summoned Absalom. So he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Absalom.

chapters.summary: Joab sent a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to bring Absalom back from exile. David permitted Absalom's return to Jerusalem but refused to see him for two years, until Absalom forced a meeting by setting Joab's field on fire.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.modern: After this Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

verses.kjv: And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
verses.modern: Absalom used to rise early and stand beside the way of the gate. And when any man had a dispute to come before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "From what city are you?" And when he said, "Your servant is of such and such a tribe in Israel,"

verses.kjv: And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
verses.modern: Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no man designated by the king to hear you."

verses.kjv: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!
verses.modern: Then Absalom would say, "Oh that I were judge in the land! Then every man with a dispute or cause might come to me. I would give him justice."

verses.kjv: And it was so, that when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
verses.modern: Whenever a man came near to pay homage to him, he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.

verses.kjv: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
verses.modern: Thus Absalom did to all of Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.
verses.modern: At the end of forty years Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.

verses.kjv: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.
verses.modern: For Your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will offer worship to the LORD.' "

verses.kjv: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.
verses.modern: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.

verses.kjv: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
verses.modern: But Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, 'Absalom is king at Hebron!'"

verses.kjv: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.
verses.modern: With Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who were invited guests. They went in their innocence and knew nothing.

verses.kjv: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counseller, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
verses.modern: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Giloh. And the conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.

verses.kjv: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.
verses.modern: A messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."

verses.kjv: And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
verses.modern: Then David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee, or else there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Go quickly, lest he overtake us quickly and bring down ruin on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."

verses.kjv: And the king's servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.
verses.modern: The king's servants said to the king, "See, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king decides."

verses.kjv: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, which were concubines, to keep the house.
verses.modern: So the king went out, and all his household after him. And the king left ten concubines to keep the house.

verses.kjv: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.
verses.modern: The king went out, and all the people after him. They halted at the last house.

verses.kjv: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
verses.modern: All his servants passed by him, all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites and all the six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath, and they passed on before the king.

verses.kjv: Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou art a stranger, and also an exile.
verses.modern: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also go with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your home.

verses.kjv: Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth be with thee.
verses.modern: You came only yesterday, and shall I today make You wander about with us, since I go I know not where? Go back and take Your brothers with You, and may the LORD show mercy and truth to You."

verses.kjv: And Ittai answered the king, and said, As the LORD liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.
verses.modern: But Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will Your servant be."

verses.kjv: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.
verses.modern: David said to Ittai, "Go then, pass on." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

verses.kjv: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.modern: All the land wept aloud as all the people passed by, and the king crossed the brook Kidron. All the people passed on toward the wilderness.

verses.kjv: And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
verses.modern: Zadok came also. All the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God until the people had all passed out of the city.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:
verses.modern: Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place.

verses.kjv: But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
verses.modern: But if He says, 'I have no pleasure in You,' here I am, let Him do to me what seems good to Him."

verses.kjv: The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.modern: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Go back to the city in peace, with your two sons, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

verses.kjv: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
verses.modern: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."

verses.kjv: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.
verses.modern: So Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem. They remained there.

verses.kjv: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
verses.modern: But David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, barefoot and with his head covered. And all the people who were with him covered their heads. They went up, weeping as they went.

verses.kjv: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
verses.modern: It was told David, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
verses.modern: When David came to the summit, where God was worshiped, there came Hushai the Archite to meet him with his coat torn and dirt on His head.

verses.kjv: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
verses.modern: David said to him, "If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.

verses.kjv: But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father's servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.modern: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I have been your father's servant in time past, so now I will be your servant,' then you will defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

verses.kjv: And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king's house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.modern: Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? So whatever you hear from the king's house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

verses.kjv: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok's son, and Jonathan Abiathar's son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
verses.modern: Their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz, Zadok's son, and Jonathan, Abiathar's son, and by them you shall send to me everything you hear."

verses.kjv: So Hushai David's friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.modern: So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.

chapters.summary: Absalom spent four years winning the hearts of the people at the gate, then declared himself king at Hebron. David fled Jerusalem with his household and loyal servants; he sent Hushai back as a spy to counter the counsel of Ahithophel.

verses.kjv: And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
verses.modern: When David had passed a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of donkeys saddled, bearing two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred of summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
verses.modern: The king said to Ziba, "Why have you brought these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who faint in the wilderness to drink."

verses.kjv: And the king said, And where is thy master's son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
verses.modern: The king said, "And where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "See, he remains in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my father.' "

verses.kjv: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
verses.modern: Then the king said to Ziba, "See, all that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." And Ziba said, "I pay homage; let me ever find favor in your sight, my lord the king."

verses.kjv: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
verses.modern: When King David came to Bahurim, there came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera, and as he came he cursed continually.

verses.kjv: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
verses.modern: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David. All the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

verses.kjv: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:
verses.modern: Shimei said as he cursed, "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!

verses.kjv: The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.
verses.modern: The LORD has avenged on You all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. The LORD has given the kingdom into the hand of Your son Absalom. See, your evil is on you, for you are a man of blood."

verses.kjv: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
verses.modern: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."

verses.kjv: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
verses.modern: But the king said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? If He is cursing because the LORD has said to Him, 'Curse David,' who then shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

verses.kjv: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.
verses.modern: David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "See, my own son seeks my life; how much more now may this Benjaminite! Leave Him alone, and let Him curse, for the LORD has told Him to.

verses.kjv: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.
verses.modern: It may be that the LORD will look on my affliction and that the LORD will repay me with good for His cursing today."

verses.kjv: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill's side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
verses.modern: So David and his men went on the road, while Shimei went along on the hillside opposite him and cursed as he went and threw stones at him and flung dust.

verses.kjv: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
verses.modern: The king. All the people who were with him, arrived weary at the Jordan. And there he refreshed himself.

verses.kjv: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
verses.modern: Now Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
verses.modern: When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

verses.kjv: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
verses.modern: Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"

verses.kjv: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
verses.modern: Hushai said to Absalom, "No, for whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, His I will be, and with Him I will remain.

verses.kjv: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father's presence, so will I be in thy presence.
verses.modern: Again, whom should I serve? Should it not be His son? As I have served Your father, so I will serve You."

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
verses.modern: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel. What shall we do?"

verses.kjv: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father's concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
verses.modern: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he has left to keep the house. All Israel will hear that you have made yourself a stench to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."

verses.kjv: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.modern: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof. And Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

verses.kjv: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
verses.modern: Now in those days the counsel that Ahithophel gave was as if one consulted the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel esteemed, both by David and by Absalom.

chapters.summary: Ziba brought provisions to David and claimed Mephibosheth had stayed behind hoping to reclaim Saul's throne. Shimei cursed David and threw stones at him as he fled, and David restrained his men from killing Shimei.

verses.kjv: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
verses.modern: Moreover, Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men. I will arise and pursue David tonight.

verses.kjv: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
verses.modern: I will come upon him while he is weary and discouraged and throw him into a panic. All the people who are with him will flee. I will strike down only the king,

verses.kjv: And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
verses.modern: I will bring all the people back to you. The man whom you seek — when all return, all the people will be at peace."

verses.kjv: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
verses.modern: The advice pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel.

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
verses.modern: Then Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what he has to say."

verses.kjv: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.
verses.modern: When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "Thus has Ahithophel spoken. Shall we do as he says? If not, you speak."

verses.kjv: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.
verses.modern: Then Hushai said to Absalom, "This time the counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good."

verses.kjv: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
verses.modern: Hushai said, "You know that your father and his men are mighty men, and that they are enraged, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Besides, your father is expert in war; he will not spend the night with the troops.

verses.kjv: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
verses.modern: Even now he has hidden himself in one of the pits or in some other place. And as soon as some of the people fall at the first attack, whoever hears it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'

verses.kjv: And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
verses.modern: Then even the valiant man, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those who are with him are valiant men.

verses.kjv: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.
verses.modern: But my counsel is that all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as the sand by the sea for multitude, and that you go to battle in person.

verses.kjv: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
verses.modern: So we shall come upon him in some place where he is to be found. We shall light on him as the dew falls on the ground, and of him and all the men with him not one will be left.

verses.kjv: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
verses.modern: If he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city. We shall drag it into the valley, until not even a pebble is to be found there."

verses.kjv: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.
verses.modern: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring harm upon Absalom.

verses.kjv: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
verses.modern: Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Thus and so did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and so have I counseled.

verses.kjv: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
verses.modern: Now therefore send quickly and tell David, 'Do not stay tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means cross over, lest the king and all the people who are with him be swallowed up.' "

verses.kjv: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
verses.modern: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel. A female servant was to go and tell them. They were to go and tell King David, for they were not to be seen entering the city.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man's house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
verses.modern: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So both of them went away quickly and came to the house of a man at Bahurim, who had a well in his courtyard. They went down into it.

verses.kjv: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
verses.modern: The woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth and scattered grain on it, and nothing was known of it.

verses.kjv: And when Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have gone over the brook of water." And when they had searched and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
verses.modern: After they had gone, the men came up out of the well, and went and told King David. They said to David, "Arise, and go quickly over the water, for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you."

verses.kjv: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.
verses.modern: Then David arose, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By daybreak not one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.

verses.kjv: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
verses.modern: When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey and went off home to his own city. He set his house in order and hanged himself. He died and was buried in the tomb of his father.

verses.kjv: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.modern: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

verses.kjv: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man's son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab's mother.
verses.modern: Now Absalom had set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had married Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

verses.kjv: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.
verses.modern: Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
verses.modern: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Machir the son of Ammiel from Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,

verses.kjv: Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
verses.modern: Brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched grain, beans and lentils,

verses.kjv: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
verses.modern: Honey and curds and sheep and cheese from the herd, for David and the people with him to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

chapters.summary: Ahithophel advised Absalom to pursue David immediately, but Hushai's counsel to delay prevailed, buying David time. When Ahithophel saw his counsel was rejected, he hanged himself; David crossed the Jordan and received supplies at Mahanaim.

verses.kjv: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
verses.modern: Then David mustered the men who were with him and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

verses.kjv: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
verses.modern: David sent out the army, one third under the command of Joab, one third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and one third under the command of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the men, "I myself will also go out with you."

verses.kjv: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.
verses.modern: But the men said, "You shall not go out. For if we flee, they will not care about us. If half of us die, they will not care about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore it is better that you support us from the city."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.modern: The king said to them, "Whatever seems best to you I will do." So the king stood at the side of the gate, while all the army marched out by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.kjv: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
verses.modern: The king ordered Joab and Abishai and Ittai, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom." And all the people heard when the king gave orders to all the commanders about Absalom.

verses.kjv: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
verses.modern: So the army went out into the field against Israel, and the battle was fought in the forest of Ephraim.

verses.kjv: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
verses.modern: The men of Israel were defeated there by the servants of David, and the slaughter there was great on that day, twenty thousand men.

verses.kjv: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
verses.modern: The battle spread over the face of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword.

verses.kjv: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
verses.modern: Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a great oak. His head caught fast in the oak. He was suspended between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him went on.

verses.kjv: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
verses.modern: A certain man saw it and told Joab, "I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak."

verses.kjv: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.
verses.modern: Joab said to the man who told him, "What, you saw him! Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? I would have been glad to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt."

verses.kjv: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
verses.modern: But the man said to Joab, "Even if I felt in my hand the weight of a thousand pieces of silver, I would not reach out my hand against the king's son, for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, 'For my sake protect the young man Absalom.'

verses.kjv: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
verses.modern: On the other hand, if I had dealt treacherously against his life (and there is nothing hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me."

verses.kjv: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
verses.modern: Joab said, "I will not waste time like this with you." And he took three javelins in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak.

verses.kjv: And ten young men that bare Joab's armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
verses.modern: Ten young men, Joab's armor-bearers, surrounded Absalom and struck him and killed him.
