verses.kjv: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
verses.modern: Then Joab blew the trumpet, and the troops came back from pursuing Israel, for Joab restrained the troops.

verses.kjv: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
verses.modern: They took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest and raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled every one to his own home.

verses.kjv: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king's dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom's place.
verses.modern: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself the pillar that is in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar after his own name. It is called Absalom's monument to this day.

verses.kjv: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.
verses.modern: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Let me run and carry news to the king that the LORD has delivered Him from the hand of His enemies."

verses.kjv: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead.
verses.modern: Joab said to him, "You are not to carry news today. You may carry news another day, but today you shall carry no news, because the king's son is dead."

verses.kjv: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.
verses.modern: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed before Joab and ran.

verses.kjv: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?
verses.modern: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why will you run, my son, seeing that you have no news ready?"

verses.kjv: But howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
verses.modern: "Come what may," he said, "I will run." So he said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and outran the Cushite.

verses.kjv: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
verses.modern: Now David was sitting between the two gates, and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall and lifted up his eyes and looked, and there was a man running alone.

verses.kjv: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
verses.modern: The watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." And he drew nearer and nearer.

verses.kjv: And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
verses.modern: The watchman saw another man running. And the watchman called to the gate and said, "See, another man running alone!" The king said, "He also brings news."

verses.kjv: And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.
verses.modern: The watchman said, "I think the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man and comes with good news."

verses.kjv: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
verses.modern: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well." And he bowed before the king with his face to the earth and said, "Blessed be the LORD Your God, Who has delivered up the men who raised their hand against my lord the king."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
verses.modern: The king said, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king's servant and your servant, I saw a great commotion. But I do not know what it was."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
verses.modern: The king said, "Turn aside and stand here." So he turned aside and stood still.

verses.kjv: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.
verses.modern: The Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "Good news for my lord the king! For the LORD has delivered You this day from the hand of all who rose up against You."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.
verses.modern: The king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And the Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you for evil be like that young man."

verses.kjv: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
verses.modern: The king was deeply moved and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he went, he said, "O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!"

chapters.summary: David's army defeated Absalom's forces in the battle of the forest of Ephraim, where 20,000 men fell. Absalom's head was caught in an oak tree, and Joab killed him despite David's order to deal gently with him; David wept for his son.

verses.kjv: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
verses.modern: It was told Joab, "See, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."

verses.kjv: And the victory that day was turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.
verses.modern: So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard that day, "The king is grieving for his son."

verses.kjv: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
verses.modern: The people stole into the city that day as people who are ashamed steal in when they flee in battle.

verses.kjv: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!
verses.modern: The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, "O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!"

verses.kjv: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;
verses.modern: Then Joab came into the house to the king and said, "You have today covered with shame the faces of all your servants, who have this day saved your life and the lives of your sons and your daughters and the lives of your wives and your concubines,

verses.kjv: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.
verses.modern: Because you love those who hate you and hate those who love you. For you have made it clear today that commanders and servants are nothing to you, for today I know that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then you would be pleased.

verses.kjv: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.
verses.modern: Now therefore arise, go out and speak kindly to Your servants, for I swear by the LORD, if You do not go, not a man will stay with you this night, and this will be worse for You than all the evil that has come upon You from Your youth until now."

verses.kjv: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.
verses.modern: Then the king arose and sat in the gate. And the people were all told, "See, the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his own home.

verses.kjv: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
verses.modern: All the people were arguing throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies and saved us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.

verses.kjv: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?
verses.modern: But Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now therefore why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"

verses.kjv: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, even to his house.
verses.modern: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Say to the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Israel has come to the king?'

verses.kjv: Ye are my brethren, ye are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
verses.modern: You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?'

verses.kjv: And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
verses.modern: Say to Amasa, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me and more also, if you are not commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.' "

verses.kjv: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.
verses.modern: He swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king, "Return, both you and all your servants."

verses.kjv: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.
verses.modern: So the king came back to the Jordan, and Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring the king over the Jordan.

verses.kjv: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
verses.modern: Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjaminite, from Bahurim, hurried to come down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

verses.kjv: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
verses.modern: With him were a thousand men from Benjamin. And Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants, rushed down to the Jordan before the king,

verses.kjv: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;
verses.modern: They crossed the ford to bring over the king's household and to do his pleasure. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was about to cross the Jordan,

verses.kjv: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
verses.modern: Said to the king, "Let not my lord hold me guilty or remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. Let not the king take it to heart.

verses.kjv: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
verses.modern: For your servant knows that I have sinned. Therefore, see, I have come this day, the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king."

verses.kjv: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD'S anointed?
verses.modern: Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered, "Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?"

verses.kjv: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?
verses.modern: But David said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be as an adversary to me? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel this day? For do I not know that I am this day king over Israel?"

verses.kjv: Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.
verses.modern: The king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king gave him his oath.

verses.kjv: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace.
verses.modern: Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had neither taken care of his feet nor trimmed his beard nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came back in safety.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest thou not with me, Mephibosheth?
verses.modern: When he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"

verses.kjv: And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant is lame.
verses.modern: He answered, "My lord, O king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said to him, 'I will saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king.' For your servant is lame.

verses.kjv: And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in thine eyes.
verses.modern: He has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the angel of God; do therefore what seems good to you.

verses.kjv: For all of my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?
verses.modern: For all my father's house were but men doomed to death before my lord the king, but you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right have I, then, to cry to the king?"

verses.kjv: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
verses.modern: The king said to him, "Why speak any more of your affairs? I have decided: you and Ziba shall divide the land."

verses.kjv: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.
verses.modern: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Oh, let him take it all, since my lord the king has come safely home."

verses.kjv: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
verses.modern: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim. He went on with the king to the Jordan, to escort him over the Jordan.

verses.kjv: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
verses.modern: Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. He had provided the king with food while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
verses.modern: The king said to Barzillai, "Come over with me. I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem."

verses.kjv: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?
verses.modern: But Barzillai said to the king, "How many years have I still to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

verses.kjv: I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
verses.modern: I am this day eighty years old. Can I discern what is pleasant and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or what he drinks? Can I still listen to the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

verses.kjv: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
verses.modern: Your servant will go a little way over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?

verses.kjv: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
verses.modern: Please let your servant turn back, that I may die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him go over with my lord the king, and do for him whatever seems good to you."

verses.kjv: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
verses.modern: The king answered, "Chimham shall go over with me. I will do for him whatever seems good to you. All that you desire of me I will do for you."

verses.kjv: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
verses.modern: Then all the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him. He returned to his own home.

verses.kjv: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.
verses.modern: The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. All the people of Judah, and also half the people of Israel, brought the king on his way.

verses.kjv: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David's men with him, over Jordan?
verses.modern: Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away and brought the king and his household over the Jordan. All David's men with him?"

verses.kjv: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king's cost? or hath he given us any gift?
verses.modern: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king's expense? Or has he given us any gift?"

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.modern: The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, and in David also we have more than you. Why then did you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

chapters.summary: Joab rebuked David for mourning Absalom while his loyal men were shamed, and David returned to Jerusalem. The tribes disputed who should escort the king back; David forgave Shimei, resolved the dispute with Mephibosheth, and rewarded Barzillai.

verses.kjv: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
verses.modern: Now there happened to be there a worthless man, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. And he blew the trumpet and said, "We have no portion in David. We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse; every man to his tents, O Israel!"

verses.kjv: So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: So all the men of Israel withdrew from David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah followed their king steadfastly from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.
verses.modern: David came to his house at Jerusalem. And the king took the ten concubines whom he had left to keep the house and put them in a house under guard and provided for them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up until the day of their death, living as if in widowhood.

verses.kjv: Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present.
verses.modern: Then the king said to Amasa, "Call the men of Judah together to me within three days, and be here yourself."

verses.kjv: So Amasa went to assemble the men of Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
verses.modern: So Amasa went to summon Judah. But he delayed beyond the set time that had been appointed him.

verses.kjv: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
verses.modern: David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, lest he get himself to fortified cities and escape from us."

verses.kjv: And there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.modern: There went out after him Joab's men and the Cherethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

verses.kjv: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab's garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
verses.modern: When they were at the great stone that is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Now Joab was wearing a soldier's garment, and over it was a belt with a sword in its sheath fastened at his hip, and as he went forward it fell out.

verses.kjv: And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
verses.modern: Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

verses.kjv: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab's hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.modern: But Amasa did not notice the sword that was in Joab's hand. And Joab struck him with it in the stomach and spilled his entrails to the ground without striking a second blow. He died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.

verses.kjv: And one of Joab's men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab.
verses.modern: One of Joab's young men took his stand beside Amasa and said, "Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab."

verses.kjv: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.
verses.modern: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the highway. And the man saw that all the people stopped. So he carried Amasa out of the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came by him stopped.

verses.kjv: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.modern: When he was taken out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

verses.kjv: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Bethmaachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.
verses.modern: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel of Beth-maacah. All the Berites assembled and followed him in.

verses.kjv: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
verses.modern: All the men who were with Joab came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah. They cast up a mound against the city. It stood against the rampart. They were battering the wall to throw it down.

verses.kjv: Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
verses.modern: Then a wise woman called from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab, 'Come here, that I may speak to you.' "

verses.kjv: And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
verses.modern: He came near her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" He answered, "I am." Then she said to him, "Listen to the words of your servant." And he answered, "I am listening."

verses.kjv: Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.
verses.modern: Then she said, "They used to say in former times, 'Let them but ask counsel at Abel,' and so they settled a matter.

verses.kjv: I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?
verses.modern: I am one of those who are peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why will You swallow up the heritage of the LORD?"

verses.kjv: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.
verses.modern: Joab answered, "Far be it from me, far be it, that I should swallow up or destroy!

verses.kjv: The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.
verses.modern: That is not true. But a man of the hill country of Ephraim, called Sheba the son of Bichri, has lifted up his hand against King David. Give up him alone. I will withdraw from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "See, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall."

verses.kjv: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
verses.modern: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. So he blew the trumpet. They dispersed from the city, every man to his home. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

verses.kjv: Now Joab was over all the host of Israel: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites:
verses.modern: Now Joab was in command of all the army of Israel. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of the Cherethites and the Pelethites;

verses.kjv: And Adoram was over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder:
verses.modern: Adoram was in charge of the forced labor. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder;

verses.kjv: And Sheva was scribe: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:
verses.modern: Sheva was secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

verses.kjv: And Ira also the Jairite was a chief ruler about David.
verses.modern: Ira the Jairite was also a chief ruler about David.

chapters.summary: Sheba the son of Bichri led a revolt against David, and the northern tribes followed him. Joab pursued Sheba to the city of Abel, where a wise woman persuaded the city to throw Sheba's head over the wall, ending the rebellion.

verses.kjv: Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the LORD. And the LORD answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.
verses.modern: Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. And David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, "There is bloodguilt on Saul and on his house, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

verses.kjv: And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
verses.modern: So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not of the people of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites. Although the people of Israel had sworn to spare them, Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the people of Israel and Judah.

verses.kjv: Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the LORD?
verses.modern: David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for You? And how shall I make atonement, that You may bless the heritage of the LORD?"

verses.kjv: And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.
verses.modern: The Gibeonites said to him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "What do you say that I shall do for you?"

verses.kjv: And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,
verses.modern: They said to the king, "The man who consumed us and planned to destroy us, so that we should have no place in all the territory of Israel,

verses.kjv: Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the LORD in Gibeah of Saul, whom the LORD did choose. And the king said, I will give them.
verses.modern: Let seven of His sons be given to us, so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD." And the king said, "I will give them."

verses.kjv: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD'S oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
verses.modern: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Saul's son Jonathan, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

verses.kjv: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:
verses.modern: The king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth. The five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite;

verses.kjv: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the LORD: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.
verses.modern: He gave them into the hands of the Gibeonites. They hanged them on the mountain before the LORD, and the seven of them perished together. They were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

verses.kjv: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
verses.modern: Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until rain fell upon them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the air to come upon them by day, or the wild animals by night.

verses.kjv: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
verses.modern: When David was told what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done,

verses.kjv: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabeshgilead, which had stolen them from the street of Bethshan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
verses.modern: David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, on the day the Philistines killed Saul on Gilboa.

verses.kjv: And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
verses.modern: He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan. They gathered the bones of those who were hanged.

verses.kjv: And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.
verses.modern: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the land of Benjamin in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. And they did all that the king commanded. And after that God responded to the plea for the land.

verses.kjv: Moreover the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.
verses.modern: There was war again between the Philistines and Israel. And David went down together with his servants. They fought against the Philistines. And David grew weary.

verses.kjv: And Ishbibenob, which was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.
verses.modern: Ishbi-benob, one of the descendants of the giants, whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of bronze, and who was armed with a new sword, thought to kill David.

verses.kjv: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.
verses.modern: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid and attacked the Philistine and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, "You shall no longer go out with us to battle, lest you quench the lamp of Israel."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was of the sons of the giant.
verses.modern: After this there was again war with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was one of the descendants of the giants.

verses.kjv: And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
verses.modern: There was again war with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, the Bethlehemite, struck down the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

verses.kjv: And there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.
verses.modern: There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. He also was descended from the giants.

verses.kjv: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimeah the brother of David slew him.
verses.modern: When he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimeah, David's brother, struck him down.

verses.kjv: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
verses.modern: These four were descended from the giants in Gath. They fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

chapters.summary: A three-year famine struck because Saul had broken Israel's oath to the Gibeonites, and David gave seven of Saul's descendants to be executed. David's mighty men killed several Philistine giants, including the brother of Goliath.

verses.kjv: And David spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day that the LORD had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:
verses.modern: David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day when the LORD delivered Him from the hand of all His enemies, and from the hand of Saul.

verses.kjv: And he said, The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
verses.modern: He said, "The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer;

verses.kjv: The God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.
verses.modern: My God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my refuge, my savior; You save me from violence.

verses.kjv: I will call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
verses.modern: I call upon the LORD, Who is worthy to be praised. I am saved from my enemies.

verses.kjv: When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid;
verses.modern: For the waves of death encompassed me, the floods of ungodly men assailed me;

verses.kjv: The sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;
verses.modern: The cords of hell entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.

verses.kjv: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my God: and he did hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry did enter into his ears.
verses.modern: In my distress I called upon the LORD; to my God I called. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry came to His ears.

verses.kjv: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of heaven moved and shook, because he was wroth.
verses.modern: Then the earth reeled and rocked; the foundations of the heavens trembled and quaked, because He was angry.

verses.kjv: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it.
verses.modern: Smoke went up from his nostrils, and devouring fire from His mouth; glowing coals flamed forth from Him.

verses.kjv: He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness was under his feet.
verses.modern: He bowed the heavens and came down; thick darkness was under His feet.

verses.kjv: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
verses.modern: He rode on a cherub and flew; He was seen on the wings of the wind.

verses.kjv: And he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies.
verses.modern: He made darkness around Him His canopy, thick clouds, a gathering of water.

verses.kjv: Through the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled.
verses.modern: Out of the brightness before Him coals of fire flamed forth.

verses.kjv: The LORD thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.
verses.modern: The LORD thundered from heaven, and the Most High uttered His voice.

verses.kjv: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.
verses.modern: He sent out arrows and scattered them; lightning, and routed them.

verses.kjv: And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
verses.modern: Then the channels of the sea were seen; the foundations of the world were laid bare, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

verses.kjv: He sent from above, he took me; he drew me out of many waters;
verses.modern: He sent from on high, He took me; He drew me out of many waters.

verses.kjv: He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
verses.modern: He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

verses.kjv: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.
verses.modern: They confronted me in the day of my calamity. But the LORD was my support.

verses.kjv: He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
verses.modern: He brought me out into a broad place; He rescued me, because He delighted in me.

verses.kjv: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
verses.modern: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He rewarded me.

verses.kjv: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
verses.modern: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.

verses.kjv: For all his judgments were before me: and as for his statutes, I did not depart from them.
verses.modern: For all His rules were before me, and from His statutes I did not turn aside.

verses.kjv: I was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity.
verses.modern: I was blameless before Him. I kept myself from iniquity.

verses.kjv: Therefore the LORD hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.
verses.modern: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight.

verses.kjv: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, and with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright.
verses.modern: With the merciful You show Yourself merciful; with the blameless man You show Yourself blameless;

verses.kjv: With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury.
verses.modern: With the pure You show Yourself pure, and with the crooked You make Yourself seem tortuous.

verses.kjv: And the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.
verses.modern: You save a humble people, but Your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down.

verses.kjv: For thou art my lamp, O LORD: and the LORD will lighten my darkness.
verses.modern: For You are my lamp, O LORD, and my God lightens my darkness.

verses.kjv: For by thee I have run through a troop: by my God have I leaped over a wall.
verses.modern: For by You I can run against a troop, and by my God I can leap over a wall.

verses.kjv: As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him.
verses.modern: This God—His way is perfect; the word of the LORD proves true; He is a shield for all those who take refuge in Him.

verses.kjv: For who is God, save the LORD? and who is a rock, save our God?
verses.modern: For who is God. But the LORD? And who is a rock, except our God?

verses.kjv: God is my strength and power: and he maketh my way perfect.
verses.modern: This God is my strong refuge and has made my way blameless.

verses.kjv: He maketh my feet like hinds' feet: and setteth me upon my high places.
verses.modern: He made my feet like the feet of a deer and set me secure on the heights.

verses.kjv: He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.
verses.modern: He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

verses.kjv: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.
verses.modern: You have given me the shield of Your salvation, and Your help made me great.

verses.kjv: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip.
verses.modern: You gave a wide place for my steps under me, and my feet did not slip.

verses.kjv: I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; and turned not again until I had consumed them.
verses.modern: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and did not turn back until they were consumed.

verses.kjv: And I have consumed them, and wounded them, that they could not arise: yea, they are fallen under my feet.
verses.modern: I consumed them; I thrust them through, so that they did not rise; they fell under my feet.

verses.kjv: For thou hast girded me with strength to battle: them that rose up against me hast thou subdued under me.
verses.modern: For You equipped me with strength for the battle; You made those who rise against me sink under me.

verses.kjv: Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
verses.modern: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, those who hated me. I destroyed them.

verses.kjv: They looked, but there was none to save; even unto the LORD, but he answered them not.
verses.modern: They looked, but there was none to save; they cried to the LORD. But He did not answer them.

verses.kjv: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, and did spread them abroad.
verses.modern: I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; I crushed them and stamped them down like the mire of the streets.

verses.kjv: Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, thou hast kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me.
verses.modern: You delivered me from strife with my people; You kept me as the head of the nations; people whom I had not known served me.

verses.kjv: Strangers shall submit themselves unto me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me.
verses.modern: Foreigners came cringing to me; as soon as they heard of me, they obeyed me.

verses.kjv: Strangers shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their close places.
verses.modern: Foreigners lost heart and came trembling out of their strongholds.

verses.kjv: The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
verses.modern: The LORD lives, and blessed be my rock, and exalted be my God, the rock of my salvation,

verses.kjv: It is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me.
verses.modern: The God Who gave me vengeance and brought down peoples under me,

verses.kjv: And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: thou also hast lifted me up on high above them that rose up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.
verses.modern: Who brought me out from my enemies; You exalted me above those who rose against me; You delivered me from men of violence.

verses.kjv: Therefore I will give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and I will sing praises unto thy name.
verses.modern: For this I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations, and sing praises to your name.

verses.kjv: He is the tower of salvation for his king: and sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore.
verses.modern: Great salvation he brings to his king, and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and his seed forever."

chapters.summary: David sang a psalm of deliverance to the LORD, celebrating God as his rock, fortress, and shield. He recounted how God rescued him from all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

verses.kjv: Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
verses.modern: Now these are the last words of David: The oracle of David, the son of Jesse, the oracle of the man who was raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet psalmist of Israel:

verses.kjv: The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
verses.modern: "The Spirit of the LORD speaks by me; His word is on my tongue.

verses.kjv: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
verses.modern: The God of Israel has spoken; the Rock of Israel has said to me: When one rules justly over men, ruling in the fear of God,

verses.kjv: And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
verses.modern: He dawns on them like the morning light, like the sun shining forth on a cloudless morning, like rain that makes grass to sprout from the earth.

verses.kjv: Although my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.
verses.modern: Although my house be not so with God, yet He hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure. For this is all my salvation and all my desire, although He make it not to grow.

verses.kjv: But the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
verses.modern: But worthless men are all like thorns that are thrown away, for they cannot be taken with the hand;

verses.kjv: But the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place.
verses.modern: The man who touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear. They are utterly consumed with fire in their place."

verses.kjv: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.
verses.modern: These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite. He raised his spear against eight hundred, whom he killed at one time.

verses.kjv: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
verses.modern: Next to him among the three mighty men was Eleazar the son of Dodo, son of Ahohi. He was with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.

verses.kjv: He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the LORD wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.
verses.modern: He rose and struck down the Philistines until His hand was weary. His hand clung to the sword. And the LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the men returned after Him only to strip the slain.

verses.kjv: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines.
verses.modern: Next to Him was Shammah, the son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered together at Lehi, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the men fled from the Philistines.

verses.kjv: But he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the LORD wrought a great victory.
verses.modern: But He took His stand in the midst of the plot and defended it and struck down the Philistines. The LORD worked a great victory.

verses.kjv: And three of the thirty chief went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam: and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.modern: Three of the thirty chief men went down and came about harvest time to David at the cave of Adullam, when a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv: And David was then in an hold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
verses.modern: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.

verses.kjv: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!
verses.modern: David said longingly, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

verses.kjv: And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the LORD.
verses.modern: Then the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate and carried and brought it to David. But he would not drink of it. He poured it out to the LORD

verses.kjv: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
verses.modern: Said, "Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this. Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" Therefore He would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

verses.kjv: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred, and slew them, and had the name among three.
verses.modern: Now Abishai the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And He wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them and won a name among the three.

verses.kjv: Was he not most honourable of three? therefore he was their captain: howbeit he attained not unto the first three.
verses.modern: He was the most renowned of the three and became their commander. But He did not attain to the first three.

verses.kjv: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow:
verses.modern: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a valiant man of Kabzeel, a doer of great deeds. He struck down two heroes of Moab. He also went down and struck down a lion in a pit on a day when snow had fallen.

verses.kjv: And he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
verses.modern: He struck down an Egyptian, a handsome man. The Egyptian had a spear in His hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed Him with His own spear.

verses.kjv: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty men.
verses.modern: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and won a name beside the three mighty men.

verses.kjv: He was more honourable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.
verses.modern: He was renowned among the thirty. But he did not attain to the three. And David set him over his bodyguard.

verses.kjv: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
verses.modern: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

verses.kjv: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
verses.modern: Shammah of Harod, Elika of Harod,

verses.kjv: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
verses.modern: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh of Tekoa,

verses.kjv: Abiezer the Anethothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
verses.modern: Abiezer of Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,

verses.kjv: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
verses.modern: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai of Netophah,

verses.kjv: Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
verses.modern: Heleb the son of Baanah of Netophah, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the people of Benjamin,

verses.kjv: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
verses.modern: Benaiah of Pirathon, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,

verses.kjv: Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
verses.modern: Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth of Bahurim,

verses.kjv: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
verses.modern: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,

verses.kjv: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
verses.modern: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,

verses.kjv: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
verses.modern: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai of Maacah, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

verses.kjv: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
verses.modern: Hezrai of Carmel, Paarai the Arbite,

verses.kjv: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
verses.modern: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,

verses.kjv: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armourbearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
verses.modern: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai of Beeroth, the armor-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,

verses.kjv: Ira an Ithrite, Gareb an Ithrite,
verses.modern: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

verses.kjv: Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.
verses.modern: Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.

chapters.summary: David spoke his last words, declaring that the Spirit of the LORD spoke through him. The names and exploits of David's mighty men are listed, including the three who broke through the Philistine lines to bring water from the well of Bethlehem.

verses.kjv: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.
verses.modern: Again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel. He incited David against them, saying, "Go, number Israel and Judah."

verses.kjv: For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.
verses.modern: So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army, who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and number the people, that I may know the number of the people."

verses.kjv: And Joab said unto the king, Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?
verses.modern: But Joab said to the king, "May the LORD Your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king still see it, but why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"

verses.kjv: Notwithstanding the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
verses.modern: But the king's word prevailed against Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the king to number the people of Israel.

verses.kjv: And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:
verses.modern: They crossed the Jordan and began from Aroer, and from the city that is in the middle of the valley, toward Gad and on to Jazer.

verses.kjv: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtimhodshi; and they came to Danjaan, and about to Zidon,
verses.modern: Then they came to Gilead, and to Kadesh in the land of the Hittites. They came to Dan, and from Dan they went around to Sidon,

verses.kjv: And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah, even to Beersheba.
verses.modern: Came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. They went out to the south of Judah at Beersheba.

verses.kjv: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
verses.modern: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

verses.kjv: And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.
verses.modern: Joab gave the sum of the number of the people to the king: in Israel there were 800,000 valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were 500,000.

verses.kjv: And David's heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O LORD, take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
verses.modern: But David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people. And David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, O LORD, please take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have done very foolishly."

verses.kjv: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,
verses.modern: When David arose in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,

verses.kjv: Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.
verses.modern: "Go and say to David, 'Thus says the LORD, Three things I offer You. Choose one of them, that I may do it to You.' "

verses.kjv: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days' pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
verses.modern: So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your foes while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days' pestilence in your land? Now consider, and decide what answer I shall return to him who sent me."

verses.kjv: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.
verses.modern: Then David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercy is great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."

verses.kjv: So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beersheba seventy thousand men.
verses.modern: So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning until the appointed time. And there died of the people from Dan to Beersheba 70,000 men.

verses.kjv: And when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshingplace of Araunah the Jebusite.
verses.modern: When the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was working destruction among the people, "It is enough; now stay your hand." And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

verses.kjv: And David spake unto the LORD when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father's house.
verses.modern: Then David spoke to the LORD when He saw the angel who was striking the people, and said, "See, I have sinned. I have done wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please let Your hand be against me and against my father's house."

verses.kjv: And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.
verses.modern: Gad came that day to David and said to him, "Go up, raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."

verses.kjv: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the LORD commanded.
verses.modern: So David went up at Gad's word, as the LORD commanded.

verses.kjv: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground.
verses.modern: When Araunah looked down, he saw the king and his servants coming on toward him. And Araunah went out and paid homage to the king with his face to the ground.

verses.kjv: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshingfloor of thee, to build an altar unto the LORD, that the plague may be stayed from the people.
verses.modern: Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, in order to build an altar to the LORD, that the plague may be averted from the people."

verses.kjv: And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what seemeth good unto him: behold, here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and other instruments of the oxen for wood.
verses.modern: Then Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good to him. Here are the oxen for the burnt offering and the threshing sledges and the yokes of the oxen for the wood.

verses.kjv: All these things did Araunah, as a king, give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, The LORD thy God accept thee.
verses.modern: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD Your God accept You."

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.modern: But the king said to Araunah, "No. But I will buy it from You for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

verses.kjv: And David built there an altar unto the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
verses.modern: David built there an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD responded to the plea for the land, and the plague was averted from Israel.

chapters.summary: David sinned by numbering the people, and God sent a plague that killed 70,000 men in Israel. David purchased the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite and built an altar there, and the plague was stopped.
